//! Generated by `semaprax::public_generic_consumer::rust_calling`. The
//! descriptor-bound FFI wrapper: ALL `unsafe` in this crate is confined to
//! this private provider module; raw declarations live in its `ffi`
//! submodule (this file's own
//! `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` overrides the package-wide
//! `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "deny"` locally, and only locally). Every
//! `unsafe` block below documents pointer provenance, length validity, the
//! native function contract relied upon, ownership before and after the
//! call, the null/output-initialization expectation, why the handle is
//! live, and who releases on failure, per issue #156's own requirement.
//!
//! This file never reimplements or modifies the native provider (issue
//! #154): every `extern "C"` signature below restates
//! `src/public_generic_abi/native/spx_pg_v1.h` exactly, and the provider
//! artifact itself is supplied externally (see `build.rs`).
#![allow(unsafe_code)]

use std::io::Write as _;

use crate::error::Error;
use crate::types::{Input, Output};

mod ffi {
    //! SAFETY (module-wide): every type and signature below restates
    //! `src/public_generic_abi/native/spx_pg_v1.h` (issue #154) exactly, a
    //! frozen versioned ABI this crate never modifies. `Raw*` types are
    //! uninhabited (`enum` with no variants), the Rustonomicon's own
    //! recommended pattern for an opaque foreign type: this crate only ever
    //! holds and passes pointers to them, never a value, so no Rust code can
    //! construct, dereference, or copy one -- exactly matching the header's
    //! own "opaque, incomplete on purpose: no public field, no copy
    //! constructor." Some named status constants below are not currently
    //! matched by name in `provider.rs` (only reached through the generic
    //! `other => Error::ExecutionFailed(other)` arm); they are kept as a
    //! complete, honest restatement of the header rather than a partial one.
    #![allow(dead_code)]

    // No `#[repr(C)]`: a zero-variant enum has no representation to fix
    // (rustc rejects `#[repr(C)]` on one outright), and none is needed --
    // this crate only ever forms and passes pointers to these types, never a
    // value, so their layout is never observed.
    pub(crate) enum RawProvider {}
    pub(crate) enum RawValue {}
    pub(crate) enum RawResult {}

    pub(crate) type Status = i32;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_OK: Status = 0;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_MALFORMED_DESCRIPTOR: Status = 1;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_DESCRIPTOR_REPLAY_MISMATCH: Status = 2;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_MALFORMED_BINDING: Status = 3;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_BINDING_REPLAY_MISMATCH: Status = 4;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_MALFORMED_CARRIER: Status = 5;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_CARRIER_CAPACITY: Status = 6;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION: Status = 7;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_HANDLE_INVALID: Status = 8;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_STICKY_SETTLEMENT_VIOLATION: Status = 9;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_ALLOCATION_FAILURE: Status = 10;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_CONTRACT_FAILURE: Status = 11;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL: Status = 12;
    pub(crate) const SPX_PG_STATUS_NULL_OR_WRONG_KIND: Status = 13;

    extern "C" {
        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_provider_open_v1(
            descriptor_bytes: *const u8,
            descriptor_len: usize,
            provider_binding_bytes: *const u8,
            provider_binding_len: usize,
            out_provider: *mut *mut RawProvider,
        ) -> Status;

        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_input_prepare_v1(
            provider: *mut RawProvider,
            carrier_bytes: *const u8,
            carrier_len: usize,
            out_input: *mut *mut RawValue,
        ) -> Status;

        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_call_v1(
            provider: *mut RawProvider,
            input: *mut RawValue,
            out_result: *mut *mut RawResult,
        ) -> Status;

        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_result_export_v1(
            result: *mut RawResult,
            out_bytes: *mut u8,
            out_capacity: usize,
            out_required: *mut usize,
        ) -> Status;

        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_result_release_v1(result: *mut *mut RawResult) -> Status;
        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_provider_close_v1(provider: *mut *mut RawProvider) -> Status;

        // Test-only surface (see docs/PUBLIC-GENERIC-CARRIER-V1.md's native
        // adapter section): never a production or publication claim. Reached
        // only through this file's own hidden `diagnostics` module below,
        // itself used only by `tests/round_trip.rs` to prove exact
        // settlement -- no other module in this crate calls these.
        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_test_inject_failure_v1(ordinal: u32);
        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_test_clear_failure_injection_v1();
        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_test_live_allocations_v1() -> usize;
        pub(crate) fn spx_pg_test_live_handles_v1(provider: *mut RawProvider) -> usize;
    }
}

/// The safe, owning handle to one open native provider. Never `Copy` or
/// `Clone`: a raw-pointer copy of this handle would let two Rust values each
/// believe they alone must close it, double-releasing the native side. Not
/// `Send`/`Sync` either -- neither derive is present, and a raw-pointer field
/// makes both auto-traits absent by default, matching the adapter's own
/// "single translation unit, single-threaded: no concurrency claim." Derives
/// `Debug` only (printing a raw pointer's address is safe and unrelated to
/// ownership duplication); never `Copy` or `Clone`.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Provider {
    handle: *mut ffi::RawProvider,
    last_release_status: i32,
}

impl Provider {
    /// Verify the exact descriptor/provider pairing, then open the native
    /// provider. Fails before any native allocation on a mutated descriptor,
    /// a mutated binding, or a provider/descriptor pairing the native side
    /// itself does not recognize.
    pub fn open(descriptor_bytes: &[u8], provider_binding_bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        // This crate's OWN independent replay, before any FFI call at all.
        crate::descriptor::verify(descriptor_bytes, provider_binding_bytes)?;

        let mut handle: *mut ffi::RawProvider = std::ptr::null_mut();
        // SAFETY: `descriptor_bytes`/`provider_binding_bytes` are borrowed
        // Rust slices, valid for reads for their full length for the
        // duration of this call; `.as_ptr()`/`.len()` is exactly the
        // `(pointer, length)` pair the header requires. `&mut handle` is a
        // valid, aligned, initialized `*mut *mut RawProvider` the callee may
        // write through; the header guarantees `*out_provider` is null on
        // any non-OK status, so `handle` is well-defined either way. No
        // ownership transfers INTO this call (both slices stay borrowed by
        // the caller); on `SPX_PG_STATUS_OK`, ownership of the minted
        // provider handle transfers OUT to the `Provider` this constructs,
        // which releases it exactly once in `Drop` below.
        let status = unsafe {
            ffi::spx_pg_provider_open_v1(
                descriptor_bytes.as_ptr(),
                descriptor_bytes.len(),
                provider_binding_bytes.as_ptr(),
                provider_binding_bytes.len(),
                &mut handle,
            )
        };
        if status != ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_OK {
            return Err(map_open_failure(status));
        }
        Ok(Provider {
            handle,
            last_release_status: 0,
        })
    }

    /// Consume `input` by value, transfer it across the native FFI boundary
    /// exactly once, call the bound endpoint, and return an independently
    /// decoded and validated `Output`. Rust's own move semantics already
    /// make reusing `input` through this safe API impossible after this
    /// call -- there is no reference, clone, or copy of it left anywhere the
    /// caller can reach.
    pub fn transform(&mut self, input: Input) -> Result<Output, Error> {
        self.last_release_status = 0;
        let outcome = self.transform_inner(input);
        // A local refusal consumes the test injection too: no state leaks into
        // the next independent call. This never retries endpoint execution.
        diagnostics::clear_failure_injection();
        outcome
    }

    /// The most recent transform's explicit release status. Zero means no
    /// release error. Inspect alongside Err to retain secondary cleanup
    /// evidence without replacing the original typed error.
    pub fn last_release_status(&self) -> i32 {
        self.last_release_status
    }

    /// Explicit close, idempotent for a closed provider. A refused native close
    /// retains its guard for retry rather than orphaning a live resource.
    pub fn close(&mut self) -> Result<(), Error> {
        if self.handle.is_null() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        // SAFETY: this exclusive borrow owns the live handle; the ABI nulls it
        // on terminal close and retains it on a retriable live-child refusal.
        let status = unsafe { ffi::spx_pg_provider_close_v1(&mut self.handle) };
        if status == ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_OK {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(Error::ReleaseFailed(status))
        }
    }

    fn transform_inner(&mut self, input: Input) -> Result<Output, Error> {
        if self.handle.is_null() {
            crate::carrier::consume_input(input);
            return Err(Error::CarrierRejected("provider is closed"));
        }
        let encoded = crate::carrier::encode_input(&input);
        crate::carrier::consume_input(input);
        let carrier = encoded?;

        let mut input_handle: *mut ffi::RawValue = std::ptr::null_mut();
        // SAFETY: `self.handle` is live (minted by a successful `open`;
        // the closed-state guard above already passed). `carrier` is a valid,
        // borrowed `Vec<u8>` for the call's duration; `.as_ptr()`/`.len()`
        // matches the header's `(pointer, length)` contract. `&mut
        // input_handle` is a valid out-pointer, null on any non-OK status
        // per the header. No ownership transfers here either: the adapter
        // copies `carrier`'s bytes into its own bounded allocation, so
        // `carrier` is simply dropped as a local when this function returns.
        // On `SPX_PG_STATUS_OK`, the minted input handle is released exactly
        // once by the very next `spx_pg_call_v1` below, which the header
        // documents as invalidating it unconditionally.
        let status = unsafe {
            ffi::spx_pg_input_prepare_v1(
                self.handle,
                carrier.as_ptr(),
                carrier.len(),
                &mut input_handle,
            )
        };
        if status != ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_OK {
            return Err(map_prepare_failure(status));
        }

        let mut result_handle: *mut ffi::RawResult = std::ptr::null_mut();
        // SAFETY: `self.handle` and `input_handle` are both live handles
        // minted by this same provider, in this same call sequence.
        // Ownership of `input_handle` transfers to the callee at this call
        // regardless of outcome (the header: "input must never be passed to
        // spx_pg_value_release_v1 after this call, succeeding or not:
        // ownership already transferred"), so this crate never releases
        // `input_handle` itself. `&mut result_handle` is a valid
        // out-pointer, null on any non-OK status.
        let status = unsafe { ffi::spx_pg_call_v1(self.handle, input_handle, &mut result_handle) };
        if status != ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_OK {
            return Err(map_call_failure(status));
        }

        let mut guard = ResultGuard { handle: result_handle };
        let outcome = export_and_decode(guard.handle);
        self.last_release_status = guard.release();
        match outcome {
            // Earlier semantic/export/codec errors stay primary.
            Err(error) => Err(error),
            Ok(output) if self.last_release_status == ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_OK => Ok(output),
            Ok(output) => {
                crate::carrier::consume_output(output);
                Err(Error::ReleaseFailed(self.last_release_status))
            }
        }
    }
}

struct ResultGuard {
    handle: *mut ffi::RawResult,
}

impl ResultGuard {
    fn release(&mut self) -> ffi::Status {
        if self.handle.is_null() {
            return ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_OK;
        }
        // SAFETY: this guard owns the sole live result. No pointer escapes to
        // safe callers. The initialized out-pointer is aligned and writable;
        // release always nulls it, including on cleanup failure. Every normal
        // outcome calls this method explicitly; Drop is only a fallback.
        unsafe { ffi::spx_pg_result_release_v1(&mut self.handle) }
    }
}

impl Drop for ResultGuard {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let status = self.release();
        if status != ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_OK {
            report_drop_failure(&Error::ReleaseFailed(status));
        }
    }
}

fn export_and_decode(result: *mut ffi::RawResult) -> Result<Output, Error> {
    let mut required = 0usize;
    // SAFETY: `result` is a live result handle owned by the caller's
    // `ResultGuard`. `out_bytes = null`, `out_capacity = 0` is exactly the
    // header's documented "query size" call: "call once with out_bytes ==
    // NULL ... to learn *out_required; the result is not consumed and no
    // byte is written." `&mut required` is a valid out-pointer the header
    // guarantees is always set.
    let status = unsafe {
        ffi::spx_pg_result_export_v1(result, std::ptr::null_mut(), 0, &mut required)
    };
    if status != ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_OK && status != ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL {
        return Err(map_export_failure(status));
    }

    if !(crate::carrier::MIN_FRAME_BYTES..=crate::carrier::MAX_FRAME_BYTES).contains(&required) {
        return Err(Error::ResultRejected("exported size is outside the bounded carrier profile"));
    }
    let mut buffer = Vec::new();
    buffer.try_reserve_exact(required).map_err(|_| Error::AllocationFailure)?;
    buffer.resize(required, 0u8);
    let mut reported = 0usize;
    // SAFETY: `buffer` is a Rust-owned allocation of exactly `required`
    // bytes, valid for writes for its whole length; `buffer.as_mut_ptr()`/
    // `buffer.len()` is consistent with that. `result` is still live (this
    // crate explicitly releases it after export/decode, which has not finished yet).
    // Nonconsuming: the header guarantees a second export call is
    // byte-identical, so no state is lost if this crate ever retried.
    let status = unsafe {
        ffi::spx_pg_result_export_v1(result, buffer.as_mut_ptr(), buffer.len(), &mut reported)
    };
    if status != ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_OK {
        return Err(map_export_failure(status));
    }
    if reported != required {
        return Err(Error::ResultRejected(
            "the writing export pass reported a different length than the sizing pass",
        ));
    }
    crate::carrier::decode_output(&buffer)
}

impl Drop for Provider {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // Normal transforms have already explicitly settled their result.
        // Drop does not replace a selected error and must not panic.
        if let Err(error) = self.close() {
            report_drop_failure(&error);
        }
    }
}

// A failed diagnostic write must never panic during destructor unwinding.
fn report_drop_failure(error: &Error) {
    let _ = writeln!(std::io::stderr().lock(), "spx-pg-rust-calling-consumer: secondary release/close failure: {error}");
}

fn map_open_failure(status: ffi::Status) -> Error {
    match status {
        ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_MALFORMED_DESCRIPTOR | ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_DESCRIPTOR_REPLAY_MISMATCH => {
            Error::DescriptorRejected(
                "the native provider's own independent replay rejected the descriptor bytes",
            )
        }
        ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_MALFORMED_BINDING | ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_BINDING_REPLAY_MISMATCH => {
            Error::ProviderMismatch(
                "the native provider's own independent replay rejected the provider-binding bytes",
            )
        }
        other => Error::ExecutionFailed(other),
    }
}

fn map_prepare_failure(status: ffi::Status) -> Error {
    match status {
        ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_MALFORMED_CARRIER => {
            Error::CarrierRejected("the native provider rejected malformed input carrier bytes")
        }
        ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_CARRIER_CAPACITY => Error::CapacityExceeded(
            "the native provider rejected an input carrier over a leaf-count or byte bound",
        ),
        other => Error::ExecutionFailed(other),
    }
}

fn map_call_failure(status: ffi::Status) -> Error {
    match status {
        ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_HANDLE_INVALID | ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_ILLEGAL_TRANSITION => {
            Error::CarrierRejected("the native provider rejected an illegal handle or lifecycle transition")
        }
        other => Error::ExecutionFailed(other),
    }
}

fn map_export_failure(status: ffi::Status) -> Error {
    match status {
        ffi::SPX_PG_STATUS_HANDLE_INVALID => {
            Error::CarrierRejected("the native provider rejected the result handle during export")
        }
        other => Error::ExecutionFailed(other),
    }
}

/// Test-only settlement-proof surface. `#[doc(hidden)]`: never part of any
/// production or publication claim (see docs/PUBLIC-GENERIC-CARRIER-V1.md's
/// native adapter section). These functions exist solely so
/// `tests/round_trip.rs` can prove zero live native allocations/handles
/// after every terminal case, success and injected failure alike.
#[doc(hidden)]
pub mod diagnostics {
    use super::super::carrier;
    use super::ffi;
    use super::Error;
    use super::Provider;

    pub fn live_allocations() -> usize {
        // SAFETY: this test-only counter takes no argument and reads
        // process-global adapter state; safe to call at any time per the
        // header's own contract for this test-only surface.
        unsafe { ffi::spx_pg_test_live_allocations_v1() }
    }

    pub fn live_handles(provider: &Provider) -> usize {
        // SAFETY: `provider.handle` is live for the duration of this
        // borrow; the counted handles all belong to this same provider.
        unsafe { ffi::spx_pg_test_live_handles_v1(provider.handle) }
    }

    pub fn inject_failure(ordinal: u32) {
        // SAFETY: takes a plain integer; arms process-global test-only
        // state for the next prepare/call/export sequence only.
        unsafe { ffi::spx_pg_test_inject_failure_v1(ordinal) }
    }

    pub fn clear_failure_injection() {
        // SAFETY: takes no argument; clears process-global test-only state.
        unsafe { ffi::spx_pg_test_clear_failure_injection_v1() }
    }

    /// Test-only access to this generated caller's own result-carrier
    /// decoder. It does not open a provider, mint a handle, allocate a
    /// native value, or invoke an endpoint; hostile bytes must fail during
    /// the decoder's full framing pass before any result leaf is copied.
    pub fn validate_result_carrier(bytes: &[u8]) -> Result<(), Error> {
        carrier::decode_output(bytes).map(|_| ())
    }
}
